FastAPI Notes
 
## What Is FastAPI
FastAPI is a modern Python web framework for building APIs. It is built on Starlette (web layer) and Pydantic (data validation). It uses Python type
It uses Python type hints to validate input, convert types and generate interactive API documentation automatically.
## Install and Run
Install with pip install "fastapi[standard]" (or fastapi and uvicorn separately). Run the development server with fastapi dev main.py or uvicorn
dev main.py or uvicorn main:app --reload. Interactive docs appear at /docs (Swagger UI) and /redoc.
## Path and Query Parameters
A path parameter is part of the URL: @app.get("/items/{item_id}") with def read(item_id: int). A query parameter is any function argument that is not
function argument that is not in the path: def read(skip: int = 0, limit: int = 10) handles /items?skip=5&limit=20. An argument with a default is
An argument with a default is optional. Invalid types return a 422 error automatically.

## Request Bodies with Pydantic
Define a model by subclassing BaseModel:
class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float
FastAPI reads the JSON body, validates it against Item and returns a clear 422 response if it is wrong. Use response_model=Item on the decorator to
on the decorator to control and filter what is returned.
## HTTP Methods
GET reads data, POST creates, PUT replaces, PATCH partly updates, DELETE removes. Use status_code=201 for created resources. Raise errors with raise
Raise errors with raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found").
## Async vs Sync
Define an endpoint with async def when it awaits non-blocking I/O (async database drivers, HTTP clients). Use a plain def for blocking code; FastAPI
for blocking code; FastAPI runs it in a thread pool so it does not block the event loop. Do not call blocking code inside async def.

...
Dependencies can depend on other dependencies and are easy to override in tests.
 
## Authentication and Security
FastAPI includes helpers for OAuth2 password flow, bearer tokens and API keys in fastapi.security. A common pattern is to issue a JWT at login and
to issue a JWT at login and read it in a dependency that returns the current user. Always hash passwords (for example with bcrypt or argon2) and
with bcrypt or argon2) and serve over HTTPS.
## Middleware, CORS and Background Tasks
Add CORSMiddleware to allow browser apps from other origins to call the API. BackgroundTasks runs small jobs (such as sending an email) after the
sending an email) after the response is returned. Use a task queue such as Celery for heavy or long-running work.
## Project Structure and Testing
Split large apps with APIRouter and include them with app.include_router(). Keep models, schemas, routers and dependencies in separate modules. Test
in separate modules. Test with TestClient from fastapi.testclient and pytest. Deploy with uvicorn or gunicorn using uvicorn workers, usually behind a
workers, usually behind a reverse proxy in a container.
## Serving an ML Model
Load the model once at startup (for example in a lifespan handler), not on every request. Accept features in a Pydantic model, call model.predict
model, call model.predict inside the endpoint and return the result as JSON.

Machine Learning Notes
 
## What Is Machine Learning
Machine learning is a way of building models that learn patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules. A model is trained on examples
model is trained on examples and then makes predictions on new data.
## Types of Learning
Supervised learning uses labeled data. Examples are classification (predict a category, such as spam or not spam) and regression (predict a number,
regression (predict a number, such as a house price). Unsupervised learning finds structure in unlabeled data, such as clustering and dimensionality
clustering and dimensionality reduction. Reinforcement learning trains an agent to maximize reward through trial and error.
## Common Algorithms
Linear regression predicts a number from a weighted sum of features. Logistic regression predicts class probabilities. Decision trees split data by
Decision trees split data by feature thresholds. Random forests average many trees to reduce overfitting. Gradient boosting builds trees one after
builds trees one after another, each fixing the errors of the last. K-means groups points into k clusters. Neural networks stack layers of weighted
stack layers of weighted sums and non-linear activations.
## Training Workflow
1. Collect and clean the data. 2. Split it into training, validation and test sets. 3. Choose features and a model. 4. Train the model on the
4. Train the model on the training set. 5. Tune hyperparameters on the validation set. 6. Evaluate once on the test set. Never tune on the test set,
Never tune on the test set, or the score will be too optimistic.
## Overfitting and Underfitting
Overfitting means the model memorizes the training data and performs badly on new data (low training error, high test error). Underfitting means the
Underfitting means the model is too simple to capture the pattern (high error on both). Remedies for overfitting: more data, simpler model,
more data, simpler model, regularization (L1 or L2), dropout, early stopping, cross-validation.
## Bias-Variance Tradeoff
Bias is error from overly simple assumptions. Variance is error from sensitivity to the particular training set. Making a model more complex lowers
a model more complex lowers bias but raises variance. The goal is the balance with the lowest total error.
## Evaluation Metrics
Accuracy is the share of correct predictions, and it misleads on imbalanced data. Precision is the share of predicted positives that are correct.
positives that are correct. Recall is the share of actual positives that were found. F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. ROC-AUC
precision and recall. ROC-AUC measures how well the model ranks positives above negatives. For regression, use MAE, MSE, RMSE and R-squared.
## Gradient Descent
Gradient descent minimizes a loss function by repeatedly moving the parameters a small step opposite to the gradient. The step size is the learning
The step size is the learning rate: too large and training diverges, too small and it is slow. Stochastic and mini-batch gradient descent use a
gradient descent use a subset of the data per step.
## Feature Engineering
Scale numeric features (standardization or min-max) for models sensitive to scale, such as k-NN, SVM and neural networks. Encode categories with
Encode categories with one-hot encoding. Handle missing values by imputing or flagging them. Avoid data leakage: never let information from the test
let information from the test set or the future influence training.
## Embeddings and Retrieval
An embedding maps text, images or other items to a vector so that similar items are close together. Cosine similarity compares embeddings.
compares embeddings. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves relevant chunks of documents by embedding similarity and gives them to a language
and gives them to a language model as context, so answers are grounded in the documents.

# Python Notes

Python is a high-level programming language.

Python is used for web development, artificial intelligence,
machine learning, automation and data analysis.
Python is also used for scripting and software development.

Popular Python frameworks include Django, Flask and FastAPI.
 
## Basics
Python is a dynamically typed, interpreted language. Indentation defines code blocks. Everything is an object, and variables are names that point to
are names that point to objects.

Common built-in types: int, float, str, bool, list, tuple, dict, set, None.
 
## Lists, Tuples, Sets and Dictionaries
A list is an ordered, mutable sequence: [1, 2, 3]. A tuple is an ordered, immutable sequence: (1, 2, 3). A set is an unordered collection of unique
collection of unique items: {1, 2, 3}. A dict maps keys to values: {"name": "Asha"}. Dict keys must be hashable, so lists cannot be keys but tuples
cannot be keys but tuples of immutable items can.
## Comprehensions
List comprehension: [x * x for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0]. Dict comprehension: {k: v for k, v in pairs}. Generator expression: (x * x for x in
expression: (x * x for x in range(10)). It is lazy and uses very little memory.
## Functions
Functions are defined with def. They support default arguments, *args for extra positional arguments and **kwargs for extra keyword arguments. Never
keyword arguments. Never use a mutable default such as def f(x=[]), because the default is created once and shared between calls. Use None and create
calls. Use None and create the list inside the function.
## Decorators and Generators
A decorator is a function that takes a function and returns a new function, applied with the @name syntax. Use functools.wraps to keep the original
to keep the original function's name and docstring. A generator is a function that uses yield. It produces values one at a time and keeps its state
at a time and keeps its state between calls.
## Classes
Classes are defined with class. __init__ initializes an instance, and self is the instance. Special methods such as __repr__, __str__, __eq__ and
__repr__, __str__, __eq__ and __len__ customize behavior. A dataclass (from dataclasses import dataclass) generates __init__, __repr__ and __eq__
__init__, __repr__ and __eq__ automatically. Inheritance is written class Child(Parent), and super() calls the parent's method.
## Error Handling
Use try / except / else / finally. Catch specific exceptions, not a bare except. Raise errors with raise ValueError("message"). A context manager
A context manager (with open(path) as f) guarantees cleanup even when an error happens.
## Modules and Environments
Import with import module or from module import name. A virtual environment isolates a project's packages: python -m venv .venv, then activate it and
.venv, then activate it and run pip install package. Pin versions in requirements.txt.
## Concurrency
The GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) lets only one thread run Python bytecode at a time. Use threads for I/O-bound work, multiprocessing for CPU-bound
multiprocessing for CPU-bound work, and asyncio (async / await) for many concurrent I/O tasks such as network calls.
## Useful Tips
Use f-strings for formatting: f"{name} is {age}". Use enumerate() to get an index and zip() to loop over several sequences. Use pathlib.Path instead
Use pathlib.Path instead of string paths. Use is to compare with None and == to compare values.
